items.name: Bacon Turkey Bravo Sandwich - Whole (1 Sandwich)

articleHtml:
At Panera Bread, the serving label can be just as important as the menu item name.

A sandwich may come as a Half or Whole. A soup may be served as a Cup, Bowl, or inside a sourdough Bread Bowl. Salads and the newer Market Bowls can use Half and Whole portions. Then You Pick Two lets you combine smaller portions from different menu categories into one meal.

Use the Panera Bread Nutrition Calculator above to choose the exact serving you order and combine sandwiches, soups, salads, bowls, bagels, bakery items, breakfast foods, drinks, spreads, dressings, and sides.

Read the Serving Size Before the Calories

Panera publishes nutrition with specific serving descriptions such as:

1/2 Sandwich

1 Sandwich

1 Cup

1 Bowl

1 Bread Bowl with soup

1/2 Salad

1 Salad

1/2 Market Bowl

1 Market Bowl

These labels should never be hidden from the user.

For example, seeing:

Bacon Turkey Bravo: 430 calories

without saying Half Sandwich gives a completely different impression from the current Whole Sandwich at approximately 860 calories .

The serving format belongs directly beside the product name.

Half and Whole Sandwiches Should Be Separate

Many Panera sandwiches have distinct Half and Whole nutrition.

The current Bacon Turkey Bravo is approximately:

Half: 430 calories, 24g protein

Whole: 860 calories, 47g protein.

The current Ciabatta Cheesesteak is approximately:

Half: 580 calories

Whole: 1,160 calories.

The Chipotle Chicken Avo Melt is approximately:

Half: 500 calories

Whole: 1,000 calories.

A Half sandwich should therefore never inherit the Whole nutrition value or rely on a hidden serving multiplier.

Use the exact published serving.

You Pick Two Is a Meal Made From Smaller Portions

You Pick Two remains one of Panera's most important meal formats.

Panera currently describes it as a way to select two entrées from categories such as:

Soups

Salads

Sandwiches

and other eligible menu items.

The final nutrition depends on the two selections.

For example:

Half sandwich + Cup of soup

is very different from:

Half salad + another Half sandwich .

There is no useful universal calorie value for “Panera You Pick Two.”

NutritionSolver should calculate the two exact portions the customer selects.

Do Not Add Two Whole Entrées to a You Pick Two

This is a common serving error.

If you choose:

Bacon Turkey Bravo + Broccoli Cheddar

inside a You Pick Two order, you generally need the eligible smaller portions associated with that meal format rather than one Whole sandwich plus one full Bowl.

NutritionSolver should therefore distinguish:

Standard/full entrée

from:

You Pick Two portion

where Panera publishes different serving sizes.

This prevents the calculator from accidentally doubling the meal.

Mix & Match Is Not the Same Thing as You Pick Two

Panera introduced a separate Mix & Match value menu in 2026.

The current version uses selected Half sandwiches, Half salads, and Cups of soup, and guests can combine multiple eligible products. Panera has also confirmed that the broader You Pick Two remains available separately.

These are two different ordering concepts.

NutritionSolver should therefore use:

You Pick Two

and:

Mix & Match

as separate meal modes when needed rather than treating the names as interchangeable.

Soup Has Three Very Different Serving Formats

Soup is one of the clearest examples of why Panera needs serving-specific nutrition.

The current Broccoli Cheddar Soup is approximately:

Cup: 280 calories

Bowl: 420 calories

Bread Bowl: 930 calories.

The Bread Bowl total is much higher because the sourdough bread itself is part of the meal.

That is not simply a large soup.

It is:

Soup + edible sourdough bowl

and should have its own record.

The Bread Bowl Alone Has a Large Nutrition Contribution

Panera's current sourdough soup Bread Bowl is approximately:

650 calories

136g carbohydrates

21g protein

before the selected soup is considered in other calculation contexts.

This explains why changing a Cup of soup into a Bread Bowl can alter the meal dramatically.

NutritionSolver should never calculate a Bread Bowl by changing only the soup portion.

The bread itself must be included.

Broccoli Cheddar Cup and Bowl Are Not Interchangeable

Current Broccoli Cheddar nutrition is approximately:

Cup: 280 calories, 8g protein, 17g carbs, 20g fat, 1,010mg sodium

Bowl: 420 calories, 12g protein, 25g carbs, 31g fat, 1,520mg sodium.

That means both calories and sodium change meaningfully with serving size.

The item title should always state:

Cup

or:

Bowl .

Mac & Cheese Has the Same Portion Problem

Panera's current Mac & Cheese is approximately:

Cup: 490 calories

Bowl: 980 calories.

It can also be served in a Bread Bowl, which creates another separate meal format.

Do not use one generic “Panera Mac and Cheese calories” figure for all three.

Salads Need Half, Whole, Protein, and Dressing Context

Panera currently publishes Half and Whole nutrition for many salads.

For example, current Caesar Salad values are approximately:

Half: 270 calories

Whole: 530 calories.

With chicken:

Half Caesar with Chicken: 340 calories

Whole: 670 calories.

The protein changes the nutrition, and dressing is also an important component.

If dressing is included in the standard published salad, do not add it twice.

If the customer swaps or adds dressing, use the selected dressing portion.

Dressing Portions Are Designed Around Half and Whole Salads

Panera's current nutrition guide publishes different dressing quantities specifically for Half and Whole salads.

For example, Caesar dressing is approximately:

Half portion: 160 calories

Whole portion: 320 calories.

Farmhouse Ranch is approximately:

Half portion: 170 calories

Whole portion: 340 calories.

This makes dressing serving size a first-class nutrition field, not a generic condiment.

Salad Stuffers Need Their Own Nutrition

Panera launched Salad Stuffers nationwide in 2026.

Instead of serving the salad in a bowl, Panera fills an Italian Stuffer Roll with the dressed salad ingredients.

The bread changes the meal substantially.

Current official nutrition examples include:

Caesar Salad Stuffer: about 650 calories

Caesar with Chicken Stuffer: about 720 calories

Fuji Apple Chicken Stuffer: about 700 calories

Green Goddess Cobb with Chicken Stuffer: about 600 calories.

A Salad Stuffer should never use ordinary salad nutrition.

It is its own serving format.

Market Bowls Added Another Half and Whole System

Panera launched a new Market Bowls category nationwide in June 2026.

Current options include:

All-In Veggie

Carnitas Elote

Sesame Ginger Chicken .

Like salads and sandwiches, these bowls have Half and Whole portions .

That means the database needs another explicit size field rather than storing one generic bowl.

Current Market Bowl Calories Vary Widely

Current official values include approximately:

All-In Veggie

  • Half: 450 calories
  • Whole: 910 calories

Carnitas Elote

  • Half: 550 calories
  • Whole: 1,100 calories

Sesame Ginger Chicken

  • Half: 470 calories
  • Whole: 930 calories.

The Whole Carnitas Elote also contains approximately 44g protein , while the Whole Sesame Ginger Chicken provides about 38g .

These should be real searchable menu records, not hidden under an old generic bowl category.

Bagel Nutrition Does Not Include Every Spread Automatically

Panera's current Asiago Cheese Bagel contains approximately:

350 calories

14g protein

55g carbohydrates

9g fat

660mg sodium .

But adding cream cheese changes the order.

Current spread examples include approximately:

Plain Cream Cheese, 1.5 oz container: 140 calories

Honey Walnut Cream Cheese, 1.5 oz: 130 calories.

So:

Asiago Bagel

and:

Asiago Bagel + Plain Cream Cheese

need different totals.

A Bagel Stack Is a Sandwich, Not Just a Bagel

Panera brought Asiago Bagel Stacks back in 2026, including breakfast and lunch/dinner versions.

Current examples include breakfast products such as:

Sausage & Egg Asiago Bagel Stack

and lunch options such as:

Chicken Roma

and:

Spicy Steak .

These contain meat, cheese, egg, sauces, vegetables, and other ingredients in addition to the bagel.

They should appear under Breakfast Sandwiches / Bagel Stacks , not ordinary Bagels & Spreads.

Breakfast Has Changed Significantly in 2026

Current Panera breakfast includes products such as:

Bacon, Egg & Cheese on Croissant

Sausage, Egg & Cheese on Ciabatta

Steak & Wake on Ciabatta

Breakfast Asiago Bagel Stacks

Avocado Toast

Soufflés

Steel Cut Oatmeal

and new crustless Frittatas .

The current Broccoli Cheddar Frittata is approximately 280 calories with 15g protein , while Five Cheese & Bacon is approximately 300 calories with 17g protein .

The breakfast database therefore needs much broader coverage than one bagel.

Croissant and Ciabatta Breakfast Sandwiches Need Separate Recipes

Changing the bread is not a small detail.

Current Panera values include approximately:

Bacon, Egg & Cheese on Croissant: 480 calories

Bacon, Egg & Cheese on Artisan Ciabatta: 470 calories

while:

Sausage, Egg & Cheese on Croissant: 620 calories

and:

Sausage, Egg & Cheese on Ciabatta: 610 calories.

The meat and bread both affect the finished sandwich.

Use the exact current product rather than estimating from one generic breakfast sandwich.

Bakery Items Need Their Own Serving Records

Panera is a bakery-café, so bakery products are a major part of the search intent.

Current nutrition includes products such as:

Blueberry Muffin: around 530 calories

Brownie: around 520 calories

Almond Pastry: around 470 calories

Pecan Braid: around 450 calories

and smaller items such as Petite Chocolate Chipper Cookies.

These should sit under a dedicated:

Bakery & Sweets

category rather than being mixed into breakfast.

A Complimentary Side Still Has Nutrition

Panera meals commonly include a side choice.

Current 2026 promotional meals mention options such as:

French Baguette

Chips

Apple

and newer premium side options.

If you eat the side, it belongs in the meal calculation.

A Half sandwich plus soup and baguette is different from the same You Pick Two with an apple.

The side should be visible in the builder.

Coffee Can Be Nearly Calorie-Free or Dessert-Like

Plain Panera coffee can contain only a few calories.

But the current beverage menu now includes flavored iced coffees, syrups, sweet cream cold foam, and Frozen Java beverages.

Panera launched its expanded cold coffee platform in June 2026 with flavors such as:

Snickerdoodle

Hazelnut Mocha

Rocky Road .

The current Café Frozen Java base is approximately:

440 calories

73g carbohydrates

65g sugar

with around 217mg caffeine for the listed 20 fl oz serving.

Do not classify every coffee as a negligible-calorie beverage.

Caffeine Belongs Beside Calories for Drinks

Panera's current official nutrition guide includes approximate caffeine amounts for beverages.

For example, a 20 fl oz light roast coffee is around 237mg caffeine , while an additional espresso shot provides approximately 63mg .

For beverages, NutritionSolver should ideally display:

Calories

Sugar

Caffeine

alongside the normal macros.

This is more useful than treating drinks exactly like sandwiches.

Location Matters at Panera

Panera explicitly states that bakery-café menus can vary because of local requirements, market testing, and availability.

The company recommends checking nutrition for the exact items available at the selected bakery-café.

NutritionSolver should therefore treat the national nutrition guide as the primary default while allowing:

location-specific availability

and, when necessary:

location-specific item variations .

Panera Bread Nutrition Questions

How many calories are in Panera Broccoli Cheddar Soup?+
How many calories are in a Panera Asiago Cheese Bagel?+
How many calories are in a Bacon Turkey Bravo?+
How does Panera You Pick Two nutrition work?+
Is a Bread Bowl the same as a Bowl of soup?+
Does Panera have half salads?+
Does Panera have bowls?+
Are bakery items included in meal calories?+

Calculate Panera by Portion, Then Build the Meal

First choose the exact sandwich, soup, salad, Market Bowl, breakfast item, bagel, or bakery food .

Then confirm whether the serving is:

Half or Whole

Cup or Bowl

Bread Bowl

or another specific Panera portion.

For a You Pick Two or Mix & Match , calculate each selected portion separately.

Finally, include the baguette, chips, apple, cream cheese, dressing, drink, coffee customization, pastry, or dessert you actually consume.

At Panera, getting the portion format right first is the key to getting the final nutrition total right.

faqs.q: How does Panera You Pick Two nutrition work?
faqs.a: You Pick Two combines two eligible entrée portions. The total depends on the Half sandwich, Half salad, Cup of soup, or other eligible portions you select.

faqs.q: Is a Bread Bowl the same as a Bowl of soup?
faqs.a: No. A Bread Bowl includes the edible sourdough bowl, which significantly increases calories and carbohydrates.
Yes. Panera's current nutrition guide publishes separate Half and Whole portions for many salads.
Yes. Panera introduced its current Market Bowls in June 2026, including Sesame Ginger Chicken, Carnitas Elote, and All-In Veggie in Half and Whole portions.

faqs.q: Are bakery items included in meal calories?
faqs.a: Only if the published meal explicitly includes them. Otherwise add the bagel, pastry, cookie, brownie, muffin, or other bakery product separately.
